record.paper_title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
record.original_question: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let G be a bounded convex domain in the complex plane, and let H(G) be the space of continuous complex-valued functions on G that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. What satisfactory precise criterion, preferably more transparent than a criterion using the full class of Green-function or Jensen-function test functions, characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(G)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
5) X = G is a bounded convex domain in C.

(5-?) At present the completeness problem has not been solved satisfactorily for any bounded convex domain G. In our article [5, Theorem 5] we give a complete solution of the completeness problem in a bounded convex domain G in terms of so-called Jensen functions.
In this theorem, the class G of Green functions plays the role of test functions. However, the class G is too wide. Some more transparent sufficient conditions can be extracted from the Theorem 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda = \{\lambda_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct nonzero complex numbers with $\lambda_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, and let $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda = \{e^{\lambda_n z}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. Let $G \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $H(G)$ denote the space of continuous complex-valued functions on the closure $\overline{G}$ that are holomorphic on $G$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\overline{G}$. The system $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda$ is said to be complete in $H(G)$ if the closed linear span of $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda$ in $H(G)$ equals $H(G)$.

Find a precise necessary and sufficient criterion, in terms of intrinsic geometric and density characteristics of the sequence $\Lambda$ and the domain $G$, for $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda$ to be complete in $H(G)$. The criterion should be more transparent than (and not simply restate) the known characterizations that quantify over the full class of Green-function or Jensen-function test functions associated to $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The completeness problem for exponential systems in a general bounded convex domain is a longstanding open problem; known characterizations exist in terms of Jensen or Green-function test classes (e.g., work of Khabibullin and collaborators), but no satisfactory transparent geometric/density criterion is known for arbitrary bounded convex domains.

status_evidence.snippet: At present the completeness problem has not been solved satisfactorily for any bounded convex domain G.
status_evidence.claim: The author explicitly states that, as of the survey, no satisfactory criterion is known for any bounded convex domain.
